title: Irreducibility and regularisation properties of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
abstract: We study regularisation and irreducibility properties of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups (GQMSs) acting on continuous-variable quantum systems. We first identify a natural notion of regularity for operators in this setting, which allows us to formulate and characterise the smoothing effects of GQMSs in terms of algebraic conditions involving the drift and quantum diffusion matrices. These conditions establish a connection with the controllability theory of quantum linear systems and with the structure of decoherence-free subsystems.   We then characterise irreducibility through several equivalent algebraic criteria: one formulated in terms of the drift and quantum diffusion matrices, one in terms of the operators appearing in the generalised GKLS representation of the generator, and a third given by a quantum analogue of Hörmander's condition. A central and somewhat surprising consequence is that, in contrast with the classical case, irreducibility is strictly stronger than conditions ensuring regularisation. Our results provide an algebraic framework for analysing these properties and lay the groundwork for a broader study of reducible Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups and, more generally, more general relevant quantum Markov semigroups on continuous-variable systems.
summary: This paper develops a deep mathematical theory characterizing the regularisation and irreducibility of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups. It establishes that these two properties are distinct, providing several equivalent algebraic criteria for each. The results offer a powerful tool for analyzing open quantum systems in continuous variable settings, particularly relevant for quantum optics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mathematical properties, specifically regularisation and irreducibility, of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups (GQMSs). It aims to establish algebraic criteria that characterize these behaviors in continuous-variable quantum systems.
main_result: The authors establish that, for GQMSs, irreducibility is a strictly stronger condition than those ensuring regularisation, leading to equivalent algebraic criteria involving the drift and quantum diffusion matrices.
method: The analysis employs advanced mathematical tools from functional analysis and quantum dynamics, comparing the quantum evolution to classical Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and utilizing superoperator formalism.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system modeled by GQMSs acting on the bosonic Fock space, relevant for quantum optics and quantum memories. The dynamics are governed by equations for the mean and covariance matrices.
key_observables: Regularisation properties, irreducibility, the decoherence-free subalgebra N(T), and the associated algebraic conditions (real CZ-cond, G-cond, Hör-cond).
important_parameters: The drift matrix (Z) and the quantum diffusion matrix (C) are central parameters determining the semigroup's evolution.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the structure of Gaussian states and the ability to translate complex quantum dynamics into equivalent linear algebraic conditions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first analyzing the classical analogy, then characterizing regularisation via the triviality of the decoherence-free subalgebra, and finally establishing the equivalence of multiple algebraic conditions (G-cond $\Leftrightarrow$ CZ-cond $\Leftrightarrow$ Hör-cond) to prove irreducibility.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous algebraic framework for analyzing open quantum dynamics in continuous variables, which is crucial for understanding decoherence and system controllability in quantum optics and quantum information processing.
